records.text: An invisible battlefield announcer whose automated calls report when siege workshops at the Broken Temple and Eastspark change hands. Its messages announce either Alliance or Horde captures.
A Swift Green Gryphon.
A Swift Red Gryphon.
A green Swift Wind Rider, a beast found in Borean Tundra.
A purple Swift Wind Rider, a beast found in Borean Tundra.
A yellow Swift Wind Rider, a beast found in Borean Tundra.
Maethor Skyshadow is a vendor in the Poison & Reagents trade. His stock serves customers seeking poisons and reagents in Northrend.

A formidable magnataur identified as Gammothra’s mate, this huntress appears among the creatures of the Borean Tundra. She fights with Tusk Strike. Her title and combat role distinguish her from an ordinary magnataur.
Nerub'ar Invaders are undead Nerub'ar encountered across several Borean Tundra areas. Their name marks them as invading forces.
The Nerub'ar Venomspitter is an undead Nerub'ar whose defining threat is its Venom Spit attack. It is encountered in the Borean Tundra.
The Nerub'ar Skitterer is an undead Nerub'ar known by its skittering role and Piercing Blow attack. It appears across multiple regions, so its identity is not tied to one locality.
Den Vermin is a humanoid creature found in Borean Tundra den areas. Its name frames it as vermin associated with a den.
A Riplash Myrmidon is a humanoid warrior of the Riplash, found in the Borean Tundra.
Steam Ragers are elemental creatures of the Borean Tundra, marked by a cosmetic steam aura and known to attack with Steam Blast.
Mammoth Calves are young mammoths found in the Borean Tundra.
Wooly Mammoths are large, woolly animals found in the Borean Tundra.
A Riplash Sorceress is a humanoid spellcaster of the Riplash, found in the Borean Tundra.

Greatfather Mahan is a taunka elder in Taunka'le Village who asks travelers to map the nerubian sinkholes troubling nearby patrols. He accepts the map but says the information will be used later, when the taunka are ready to act.

Chieftain Wintergale defends Taunka'le Village against Scourge pressure from En'kilah. He puts his people's survival ahead of glorious death in battle, choosing Sage Aeire's plan for a concealed infiltrator over Durm's blind assault. He argues that a chieftain must weigh more than personal honor, invoking the lives of warriors and Greatfather Mahan, who raised Durm.

Durm Icehide urges a direct attack on En'kilah despite unfavorable odds, calling Wintergale cowardly for following Sage Aeire's stealth plan. Durm prizes dying with axes in hand rather than going quietly to slaughter, and considers the scheme dishonorable. Yet Durm also welcomes capable allies helping the village evacuate before the Scourge overruns it.

Sage Aeire is a Taunka sage trusted by Chieftain Wintergale to help carry out his plans against the Scourge at En'kilah. She prepared a totem using ancient magic to neutralize the plague cauldrons, knowledge she says the sages have largely stopped using. She also draws on ancestral knowledge of confusing enemies' senses, hoping to expose Scourge weaknesses or strike their commanders. Her remarks show concern for the chieftain's resolve and confidence in the Taunka's ability to defeat the Scourge.

Wind Tamer Barah is a Taunka elemental worker helping defend Taunka'le Village from the Scourge. She knows how to use elemental hearts and the Horn of Elemental Fury to create and bind an elemental capable of collapsing Nerubian tunnels. She is cautious about the horn's uncertain legend, but committed to using it against the assault. Barah honors Stormhoof, who died securing the horn, and says she will safeguard it after the fighting; she hopes to visit his tomb on pilgrimage when the Scourge threat is dealt with.

Snow Tracker Junek is a Taunka tracker at Taunka'le Village. After hearing what happened to Grumm, whom the Scourge captured and tortured, Junek says she feared he had been taken but had not imagined the cruelty inflicted on him. She honors him as a mighty warrior and says his people will remember him that way.
A dragonkin watcher associated with the Nexus in Borean Tundra, using Intangible Presence against nearby foes.

Surristrasz is a dragonkin at Amber Ledge who watches mortals’ efforts and regards their Dalaran concerns as trivial beside the danger to the world’s future. He helps reforge the key needed to free Evanor, yet fiercely protects his drakes and holds their riders accountable for any harm. He sends visitors to Coldarra to confront the threat firsthand and meet Archmage Berinand.
A target for mage hunters.
A Cult of the Damned plaguebringer can cast Ghoul Summons while out of combat and Plague Cauldron Beam.

King Mrgl-Mrgl is a D.E.H.T.A. observer who studied Winterfin life in disguise and reluctantly took charge of the unaffected murlocs after a landslide exposed caverns and a makrura’s influence. He fears his true nature being exposed, works to secure the Winterfin’s future, and investigates the caverns’ magic, which he sees as part of the spreading Nexus War.

Winterfin gatherers expect help collecting clams and killing orcas. Their speech expresses concern for village kin who have lost their reason, resentment toward outsiders, unease about entering the caves and suspicion of the new King Mrgl-Mrgl.

Brglmurgl is a Winterfin at the retreat whose people have been driven from their village and lost tadpoles and kin to the murlocs across the water. He demands that outsiders prove themselves by striking those “betrayers,” and remains unimpressed even after they learn to speak with the Winterfin.
Glrggl is identified by the Winterfin as the king of the Glimmer Bay orcas and the target of their campaign against the orcas attacking them.

Mrmrglmr is a Winterfin who agreed to clean King Mrgl-Mrgl’s things, then kept the king’s spare murloc costume and threatened to expose him. He bargains by returning it in exchange for the king’s continued help against their enemies. He also wants Glrggl’s head, expecting the orca king’s death to reduce attacks and provide a feast.

Ahlurglgr is the Winterfin’s surviving clam merchant. Suspicious when an outsider first offers clams, he accepts the gift once reassured and invites the visitor to trade again. His wares and role are tied to the Winterfin’s high regard for clams.

Lurgglbr is a captive Winterfin who asks for help escaping the caverns. Defiant toward his captors, he believes his brothers and sisters have been driven mad and calls them brainwashed. After reaching safety, he thanks his rescuer and asks that the king be told he is back.

Claximus is a lobstrok whom King Mrgl-Mrgl blames for stealing Winterfin tadpoles and controlling murlocs after they entered the caverns. Mrgl-Mrgl calls for Claximus’s death and asks for a claw as proof.
Keymaster Urmgrgl is a keymaster in the Winterfin Caverns. Glrglrgl says Urmgrgl holds the key to his cage. Urmgrgl jokes with passersby, “I am the Keymaster. Are you the Gatekeeper?”
Cleaver Bmurglbrm calls out beside a dead whale and asks travelers for orca blubber. He says he has carcass-cutting to do and offers leftover stew in return for the blubber.
Winterfin Shorestrikers are murloc combatants found around Winterfin territory. They charge with Rushed Assault and may flee for help when badly hurt.
Winterfin Oracles are murlocs found around Winterfin territory. In combat, they may run away in fear and cast a bolt.

A Winterfin murloc warrior and combatant in the conflict around Winterfin Retreat. The Winterfin say their rivals across the water kidnapped their tadpoles, drove them from their village, and killed many of their people; warriors like this one are among the targets in that fighting.

Recruitment Officer Carven handles recruitment for the barracks, asking newcomers about their profession and sword skills before directing them to duty. His remarks suggest a practical recruiter with quotas to fill: he jokes about a mistaken headcount, issues equipment when needed, and sends capable recruits to the front lines.

Scalder is a female elemental of air and watery fury dwelling in a trench below Winterfin Retreat. King Mrgl-Mrgl describes her as a source of magical steam and asks adventurers to defeat her so he can capture it for his effort to teach them the Winterfin dialect.
A Crypt Crawler is an undead Nerubian found in the Sands of Nasam outside Valiance Keep. Sergeant Hammerhill’s account of the siege identifies these crawlers as targets in the fighting there.
A Risen Crypt Lord is an undead Nerubian in the Sands of Nasam area outside Valiance Keep, part of the same local threat as the Crypt Crawlers.
A Stormfleet Deckhand is a humanoid deckhand found in the Borean Tundra’s Stormfleet area.

Hilda Stoneforge receives ore shipments at Valiance Keep for making weapons. When Gerald’s final Farshire ore delivery arrives, she is surprised because the shipment was not yet scheduled; Gerald describes her as a good friend and asks that she make weapons from the ore as Farshire prepares to defend its land.

Garrosh Hellscream commands the Warsong Offensive in Northrend, intent on marching to Icecrown and reserving soldiers for the main conflicts. He dismisses Saurfang's concerns about shipping and supplies, trusting the Horde's warrior spirit and rejecting warnings about consequences. Yet he remembers help given to his people in Nagrand: acknowledging that debt, he offers that helper a chance to leave the dangerous campaign.

During the Scourge attack, Gamlen calls people to the town hall, announces that weapons have arrived, and urges them to arm themselves and fight back. His recorded words present him as a rallying voice for the settlement's defense.
Thulrin is a named humanoid who follows a route.
Bromm is a humanoid in Borean Tundra.
Gelrynd is a humanoid in Borean Tundra.
A Warsong battleguard in Borean Tundra who pledges a life to the Horde, welcomes its champion and considers serving alongside that champion an honor.
A Warsong honor guard in Borean Tundra who pledges a life to the Horde and regards serving alongside its champion as an honor, greeting the champion’s return with respect.
A Warsong marksman in Borean Tundra who engages enemies with shooting attacks.

James Deacon keeps the inn at Valiance Keep, where supplies have grown limited after months without a shipment. He directs military inquiries to the retired marine Colburn and seeks the Kul Tiras wine that helps the veteran talk. James warns on-duty servicemen against drinking for fear of the general’s anger, but also gives in while asking them to keep his involvement quiet.

Endorah is distressed that others do not believe her account of an attempted abduction. While gathering herbs near the rift, she says dark wizards and magical beasts surrounded her and a floating box drew her inside. Riders on red drakes rescued her before it closed. Grateful and awestruck, she asks that her thanks be delivered to Amber Ledge.

At Valiance Keep, “Salty” John Thorpe poses as a kitchen worker, but his words on exposure reveal an operative of the Cult of the Damned. He invokes Arthas, threatens death, and says he will not go down quietly.

Midge is a herb gatherer who says dark wizards captured her near the rift with a magical cube, before drake-riding rescuers interrupted them and she escaped. Though frustrated that others doubt her account, she wants the people who saved her thanked for their help.

General Arlos is a senior officer at Valiance Keep who receives reports and welcomes arriving recruits to Northrend. When told of cultist activity among the settlements, he thanks the messenger and says Counselor Talbot considers the incident isolated and not a military concern.

Leryssa came to Valiance Keep searching for her brother Thassarian, whom she believed had died years earlier. After learning he enlisted there, she investigates through William Allerton and an enlistment ledger, and suspects William’s death was not random. When she finds Thassarian alive, her relief and fear are plain: she begs him not to leave her again and worries that the army sent him to die.
Valiance Keep footmen serve as the keep’s military guards, stationed around the keep and nearby area.

High Overlord Saurfang worries about fighting a fearless Scourge and the Horde's strained resupply routes in Northrend. He warns Garrosh against impatience and recklessness, recalling that he drank Mannoroth's cursed blood as Garrosh's father did. In the account of his son's death, Saurfang expresses grief but also pride in an honorable end, arranging for the returned armor to accompany the funeral pyre in Nagrand.

Footman Rob is a named footman in Borean Tundra who jokes with his companions over a last drink before they head to the front, acknowledging they might not return. During the scene, he summons the separately named Footman Mitch.
Footman George is a named footman in Borean Tundra. In a brief exchange, he gives a casual, willing-sounding “Sure, why not?”
Footman Chuck is a named footman in Borean Tundra with a blunt complaint about the beer, calling it the worst he has ever had.

Librarian Donathan is a loyal representative of Dalaran at Amber Ledge, recruiting help to investigate abducted mages. He urgently seeks Lady Evanor’s rescue, arranges the capture of a Beryl sorcerer for questioning and prepares a way through Salrand’s shield. He considers rescue a duty, yet regrets the unpleasant work desperation has led him to request.
Julia Celeste holds the title of justicar and is stationed in Borean Tundra.
A worker at Valiance Keep.

Sauranok the Mystic fears that something terrible has happened to his old friend, Farseer Grimwalker, after sensing a disturbance and clutching his chest. He directs help to Spirit Talker Snarlfang, Grimwalker’s pupil, who accompanied the farseer north to establish an outpost near Sholazar Basin and may know what happened.
The Warsong Recruitment Officer is a Horde quest giver stationed in Warsong Hold. The role is to welcome arriving recruits and direct them to the hold’s leadership.

Armorer Orkuruk is a blacksmith and a blunt, demanding foreman. He berates workers for shoddy equipment, slow work, and poor hammering, and pushes them to keep the weapons coming. He also offers goods to browse.
A Warsong blacksmith posted in Warsong Hold, identified by the trade and faction in its name.
A goblin siege engineer stationed in Warsong Hold, identified by the engineering role and siege focus in its name.
Chief Engineer Leveny is a Grand Master Engineer in Warsong Hold.
Williamson is an innkeeper in the Borean Tundra who invites weary visitors to rest. The inn offers a home hearthstone option and goods to browse.

Overlord Razgor treats the Nerubian attack on Mightstone Quarry as a direct threat to Warsong Hold, with the Scourge massed beyond it. He sends soldiers to kill Nerubians and destroy their eggs, warning that their numbers are growing despite the defenders’ efforts. He also directs a capable fighter toward the Scourge threat and onward to Wind Master To’bor.

Foreman Mortuus sees the Scourge’s capture of Warsong peons as a threat to construction: without their labor, work stops. His appeal for help is edged with contempt, calling the peons foolish and weak, while his report afterward says most returned and credits the rescue. He directs the player to free those webbed across Mightstone Quarry.
Heldgarr Steelbeard is a named combatant who shoots even while out of combat. He is in the Borean Tundra region.
Ferlynn Windsong is a named combatant who shoots even while out of combat. She is in the Borean Tundra region.
A Nerub'ar Victim in Borean Tundra.

Harbinger Vurenn is a named military figure who doubts the general’s account and pursues intelligence on cultists aiding the Scourge near Valiance Keep. Suspecting that someone inside may serve the cult, he entrusts evidence to an operative to take discreetly to Vindicator Yaala. He also offers the general military support from his people.
One of the Warsong Wind Riders in the Borean Tundra, this rider answers a superior with a brief, dutiful “Yes sir!”
Turida Coldwind is a named Wind Rider Master whose travel service lets visitors travel fast. When attacked, she calls for guards and summons an Enraged Wyvern.
Wind Master To’bor is a named wind rider who greets an expected arrival and points west toward the danger across the tundra. His dialogue also calls for lift-off.

Librarian Garren is a Dalaran researcher stationed at Amber Ledge to chart and monitor newly appearing energy anomalies in the Borean Tundra. He relies on instruments and field readings, and asks others to collect data while he compiles notes and reports for his colleagues and the Dalaran council. His formal, measured manner gives way to urgency when a major disruption is detected. He can provide water breathing for underwater investigation.

Etaruk is a former craftsman of the Coldrock Quarry and a member of its people, whose companions were preparing statues for their last rites when mage hunters invaded. He fears the invaders will destroy the statues and steal the community's artifacts. He speaks of his people in Kaskala and their allies, and sees the quarry's defense as a shared struggle; reverence for the ancestors shapes his gratitude toward those who help.
Nerub'ar Web Lords are nerubian creatures found in several areas of the Borean Tundra. In combat, they cast Blinding Swarm.

Captain “Lefty” Lugsail receives a report that Cult of the Damned fanatics have reached Northrend and reacts angrily at the thought of his crew letting them aboard. He refers the danger to Admiral Cantlebree. Their exchange places him in Valiance Keep’s naval command and shows a captain concerned about security aboard ship.

Admiral Cantlebree treats the report of Cult of the Damned activity as a wider security threat. She calls for General Arlos to be notified, warns that cultists may have been smuggled into other Northrend settlements, and describes Captain Lugsail as unusually careful. Her concern extends beyond her own ship to the safety of Alliance settlements.
A Draenei delegate in Borean Tundra.

Counselor Talbot presents himself as an adviser to Valiance Keep’s command and directs an adventurer to help Karuk, a young tuskarr seeking aid. In secret, he serves the Scourge: he reports that its influence within the Alliance is growing, claims power over human minds, and offers captured intruders to his master. His helpful public role masks a dangerous allegiance.

Old Man Colburn is a retired marine whose life still revolves around the military. He knows the names of generals, units, brigades and detachments, and Kul Tiras wine recalls his days with the lads at the barracks. His memory is scarred, and he may stare blankly; he is also connected with a deserter held in the keep’s prison.
Valiance Keep’s cannoneers are its artillery crew, stationed in the keep. Several are present, reflecting a shared military role rather than an individually identified character.

Recruitment Officer Blythe is a senior officer at Valiance Keep who handles enlistment. With the recruitment ledger missing, Blythe directs a particularly capable prospective recruit to General Arlos instead of the ordinary queue, citing that recruit’s record in Outland.
Valiance Keep Riflemen are the keep’s ranged soldiers, found around its nearby grounds. They fire their guns while out of combat, marking their role as ranged fighters among the garrison.
Valiance Keep Footmen are the keep’s foot soldiers, encountered around the keep and its nearby grounds. They form part of the local garrison.

Archmage Berinand researches the Nexus crisis from the Transitus Shield. Fascinated by Azeroth’s ley lines being drawn to the Nexus, he nevertheless focuses on slowing the dimensional rift and studying how its energies transform the Glacial Ancients. He asks for samples and evidence from within the Nexus, hoping to buy time against Malygos; after the player’s aid, he thanks them and says Dalaran will hear of their service.
Beryl Sorcerers are arcane combatants found around Beryl Point and Coldarra.

Civilian Recruits are gathered in a line at Valiance Keep. One complains that his arm is getting sore and says the activity is harder than it looks; another challenges a passing player for acting too good to wait with the rest.

The Kaskala craftsmen were innocent quarry workers murdered in the attack, their spirits left imprisoned by beryl hounds. One freed craftsman thanks the rescuer and asks that Kaskala remember what happened.

The Kaskala shamans were among the innocent workers murdered in the attack, their spirits left in chaos and imprisoned by beryl hounds. A freed shaman thanks the rescuer and wishes them the aid of the ancestors and safe passage on the winds and seas.

Overlord Bor'gorok leads the Horde outpost at Bor'gorok. After Steeljaw's caravan disturbed taunka burial grounds and its spirits rose, Bor'gorok warns that the Horde's conduct will shape its relations with the taunka, but welcomes help against Steeljaw's spirit. He later thanks the player for restoring those relations.

Quartermaster Holgoth oversees Warsong munitions at Warsong Hold and directs efforts to recover explosives from Nerubian occupied ground and collapse nearby sinkholes. He is brisk and pressed for time; he jokes that his calculations are often wrong and voices uncertainty that the charges will stop the Nerubians.

Shadowstalker Luther was one of Varimathras’s best field agents, sent to spy on the Nerubians near Mightstone Quarry. His journal reports a Scourge spawning glade and says he tried to flee after suspecting they had discovered him. He poisoned himself rather than be captured; the Nerubians left his toxic corpse alone.

Gorge the Corpsegrinder is a Horde tank commander overseeing the siege tanks at Garrosh’s Landing and the fight against the Scourge. He sends tank crews to attack Scourge forces and rescue Warsong soldiers, with orders to report success to Garrosh Hellscream. He openly hates gnomes and threatens Mobu, while the coastal mist visibly unsettles him.
An undead Stitched Warsong Horror from the Plains of Nasam. During the siege-tank assault, destroying one can count toward the Scourge Soldier objective.
An undead aggressor from the Plains of Nasam. During the siege-tank assault, destroying one can count toward the Scourge Soldier objective.
A Horde siege tank: a non-humanoid war machine that responds to a hit from the Fuel spell by announcing that it gains fuel.

Longrunner Proudhoof is a taunka leader at the sacred burial grounds, grieving the disturbance of his ancestors. He rallies an assault on Steeljaw's caravan and its commander’s cursed spirit, urging the raiders to return the dead to rest. He directs survivors north to report to Overlord Bor'gorok.

Grunt Ragefist is a Horde grunt sent by Overlord Bor'gorok to help Longrunner Proudhoof at Steeljaw's Caravan. He treats the fallen caravan workers as Horde dead who deserve an honorable funeral, and insists their bodies be burned rather than left on sacred taunka ground. He blames the disaster on Steeljaw's foolish shortcut and calls on Horde pride to help clean up the mess.
A rank-and-file Warsong caravan guard, one of the armed escorts associated with the supply caravan at Steeljaw's Caravan.

Spirit Talker Snarlfang is a spirit talker at Bor'gorok Outpost who works with the spirits and performs rituals involving primal essences. He urges haste when an essence is at risk and laments when a spirit is shackled.

A dead guard of Steeljaw's caravan, serving with the Warsong Offensive, lies in the cemetery on sacred taunka ground. The fallen guards and workers are to be honored with a funeral pyre; this corpse can also be searched for clothing.

A dead worker of Steeljaw's caravan, serving with the Warsong Offensive, lies in the cemetery on sacred taunka ground. The fallen workers and guards are to be honored with a funeral pyre; this corpse can also be searched for clothing.
A Scourge Plague Spreader in Borean Tundra.
A Risen Longrunner is an undead longrunner whose combat routine uses Ghost Strike.
A taunka spirit disturbed when Steeljaw's caravan crossed a burial mound. Longrunner Proudhoof asks for his ancestors' spirits to be laid to rest, and Ghostly Sages are among those taunka spirits.
One of the mages carried to Coldrock Quarry on mysterious blue platforms. The treasure hunters murdered Etaruk's companions and plundered the quarry, threatening the taunka's statues and artifacts.
A hound found around Coldrock Quarry and nearby Beryl Point.

A warmage at Amber Ledge directing the effort to free Lady Evanor at Beryl Point. Anzim asks for Salrand's Key and sends the player with his war mages; he warns that he will hold them accountable if one of his drakes is harmed.
A humanoid identified as an Alliance deserter, found in the Borean Tundra.
A swine found in the Borean Tundra.
A red drake guarding the frozen wastes around the Borean Tundra.

Ortrosh is a wounded orc at Bor'gorok Outpost who believes he should have died alongside the farseer at Magmoth. He sees the attack as a dishonor and urges revenge against the magnataur and their snobold servants to restore the outpost's honor. His words also show that he is recovering from his wounds and doubts his return to being the warrior he was.

Imperean is a powerful elemental who speaks with authority and condescension toward mortals. The ongoing war between fire and water enrages its vassals; Imperean seeks to end their quarrel and treats the resulting motes as a resource. It offers help with the farseer's situation in exchange for assistance, and presents keeping its word as a matter of honor, even to a mortal.
A brittle skeleton, an undead creature.
An undead Cult of the Damned necromancer at En'kilah, this enemy is among the forces the Taunka seek to drive from the Temple City. It casts a necrotic purple beam while out of combat.

Warden Nork Bloodfrenzy oversees prisoners at the internment camp southeast of Warsong Hold and directs their escort and exchange. He treats Alliance deserters with open contempt, calling them cowards, yet insists they remain soldiers and sworn enemies of the Horde. He also says they surrendered their arms and armor, and orders an escort to keep up appearances with the Alliance.

A Horde soldier on the southern front at Bloodspore Plains, Primal Mighthorn works with Bloodmage Laurith on Hellscream’s magnataur mission. Their platoon was wiped out in its first assault, leaving the two to continue the operation. Mighthorn focuses on weakening magnataur with bloodspore powder.

A bloodmage and field researcher at Bloodspore Plains, Laurith studies how bloodspore plants and moths sustain the local ecology. She is excited by her discoveries and readily draws others into the work, even asking a volunteer to test a flower directly on their skin while she observes.
An En'kilah Abomination is an undead abomination whose combat routine uses Cleave.

William Allerton was a family friend of Thassarian, who says William told him that his brother enlisted the same day. Thassarian also reports that William was stationed at Farshire mine. William's throat was cut, and an enlistment card bore his name; his corpse had no bite or claw marks.
An En'kilah crypt fiend that casts Crypt Scarabs in combat.
An En'kilah gargoyle.
An En'kilah hatchling.
High Priest Andorath is one of the Scourge high priests of En'kilah. The priests command Scourge forces and hold the scrolls tied to entering Naxxanar; Andorath's scroll is at the Spire of Blood.
An En'kilah ghoul is a creature targeted among the forces in the Temple City. It fights with Flesh Rip.

Shadowstalker Barthus is a field agent serving Varimathras, tasked with spying and occasional assassination. He investigates Nerubian activity and discovers Scourge farms used to create more forces. After reading Luther's journal, Barthus calls the news very bad and says Garrosh Hellscream must be notified; he plans to send scouts and requests reinforcements.

Private Brau is a soldier connected to Thassarian's operation against the Scourge. He considers the plan to storm a Scourge ziggurat near a plagued Nerubian city reckless, and says the group was meant to arrange passage east with Ataika in Kaskala.
An undead skeletal mage of Naxxanar who fights with Frostbolt, threatens an opponent’s approaching death and boasts that its enemies cannot stop them all.
The Enraged Tempest is an elemental in Borean Tundra that uses Enrage when wounded.

Simmer is an elemental at the Charred Rise who has fought with Churn over the boiling of Churn’s pool. Simmer is willing to consider an armistice if Churn stops the watery intrusions, but remains hostile to intruders and warns them away.
Raging Boilers are elemental creatures found near the boiling pools. They attack intruders with scalding steam.
Churn is an elemental whose pool is boiled by Simmer. Churn agrees to an armistice if Simmer stops, but warns intruders away after submitting.
Boiling Spirits are elemental creatures in the area around Blistering Pool. They attack intruders with scalding steam.
Mystical Webbing.

Farseer Grimwalker's Spirit is a shaman spirit inside Magmoth who says Kaganishu killed him and bound him there with a fetish made from his body. He says Kaganishu is using the fetish to learn shamanism and asks for it to be recovered so he can be freed. The spirit also expresses gratitude for temporary reprieve while making clear that this is not true freedom.

Ug’thor Bloodfrenzy is called “popo” by a companion and wonders aloud whether unfamiliar creatures are pigs, whether they are cowardly, and what they fear or are doing here. His questions and confused pauses, along with scratching his head and puffing out his chest to stand on tiptoe, make him seem uncertain but eager to understand.

Kaganishu is a snobold shaman at Magmoth. Farseer Grimwalker’s spirit identifies him as the one who ritually murdered him and made a fetish from his body to learn shamanism; the spirit remains tethered there by that fetish. Bonker Togglevolt also names Kaganishu as the snobolds’ main shaman. He attacks with fire and a close-range blast.

Magmoth Shamans serve among the snobolds at Magmoth, where they are part of the force opposing the Bor’gorok Outpost. When attacked, they shout phrases that include Kaganishu’s name and Magmothregar’s, marking ties to those figures; their cries also include “Kada nu batteka, oht!”

Magmoth Foragers are snobolds at Magmoth, counted among the force opposing the Bor’gorok Outpost. When attacked, they shout the same calls heard from the shamans, including Kaganishu’s and Magmothregar’s names. Their cries give them a place in the group’s shared allegiance and responses.

Magmothregar is the magnataur chieftain at Magmoth. Crafty Wobblesprocket identifies him as the target of her disguise-and-banner scheme, intended to turn the Warsong orcs’ attention toward the magnataur. Magmoth Shamans and Foragers call his name when attacked, indicating his importance among them.
A Kaskala Ancestor in Borean Tundra.
At Magmoth, Mate of Magmothregar is a beast identified among the magnataur targets in the Horde outpost's revenge campaign. It can enter a frenzy when badly wounded.
A humanoid known as Offspring of Magmothregar, found in Borean Tundra.
Magmoth Crusher is a magnataur found at Magmoth and named among the targets in the Horde outpost's revenge campaign.

Karuk is a young tuskarr survivor of Pal'ea, where the Kvaldir destroyed his village and killed his father Ariut and others he knew. He describes himself as a fisherman who has not yet passed the test of manhood, and says tuskarr law obliges him to seek retribution for his kin. Unable to face the Kvaldir himself, he asks for help carrying out that blood duty, including against Gamel the Cruel, whom he names as his father's killer. He has only heard that the captive naga priestess Veehja may shed light on a mystery involving his father; he presents her cooperation as a possibility, not something he knows.

Shadowstalker Ickoris is a Horde operative at Warsong Farms Outpost investigating the Scourge's use of the farms to transform captured soldiers into undead. The discovery that the monsters were once orcs and tauren visibly disturbs him, and he wants more information before deciding how to respond.

Shadowstalker Canarius works at Warsong Farms Outpost, where Horde soldiers held in cages are beyond the outpost's reach while necrolords and aberrations guard them. He asks for help recovering keys and freeing prisoners, treating each rescued soldier as one fewer undead threat and a service to the Horde.

Scout Tungok is a Horde scout whose work around the Bloodspore Plains includes clearing kobolds from the fields. He calls the kobolds vermin and complains that their stink makes his life miserable; he finds the job unpleasant too.
A Nerub'ar Corpse Harvester, it attacks with Venom Spit when in combat.

A Warsong Captain who rallies the soldiers against the Lich King's forces. He urges one soldier to settle down and tells another they will be ready after being warned; he declares that the Horde will not relent.

Curator Insivius leads the mage hunter forces and oversees their operation from a flying disk on the quarry's upper rim. Etaruk describes him as a fearsome creature unlike anything his people have seen; Insivius attacks with a charge and Frost Nova.
Beryl Reclaimer is a humanoid found in Borean Tundra.

Veehja is a naga priestess of the scale seeking vengeance on the Kvaldir occupying Riplash. She says they sacrificed naga and tuskarr to awaken Leviroth, undoing Queen Azshara's work. Disgusted by relying on outsiders, she nevertheless asks for the Trident of Naz'jan from Ragnar so the beast can be slain, then wants her helper to leave her alone.
The Scourged Mammoth is an undead mammoth that attacks by trampling its foes.

Ith'rix the Harvester is an undead Scourge agent who anticipates pleasure in tearing the Horde's forces apart. A fragment of Ith'rix's hardened carapace is sought as a trophy to present to High Overlord Saurfang at Warsong Hold.
The Tundra Crawler is a beast that attacks with corrosive poison.

At Warsong Hold, Yanni is a blond elf who arranges carpet trips to Garrosh’s Landing. He devised the carpet route after Scourge attacks made wind-rider scouting perilous, and describes it as safer for passengers while admitting the rider remains at risk.
Bloodspore Moths are beasts found across several Borean Tundra areas; when fighting, they can use Wing Buffet.

Kel'Thuzad taunts opponents that resistance only delays the inevitable. This undead figure announces a dread citadel rising in the east and armies of the dead marching from Icecrown, presenting their advance as unavoidable. Kel'Thuzad also casts Unholy Frenzy.

A Bloodspore Harvester, one of the ratlike people Scout Tungok calls vermin, pleads not to harm the lifegiver or touch the spores and urges others to protect them. Its words and its Bloodspore Malaise fit a defensive concern for its people’s source of life.

A Bloodspore Roaster shares its people’s pleas to protect the lifegiver and spores. It tends to roasting even outside combat and uses Roast when fighting, giving its role a clear culinary and combat edge.
A Bloodspore Firestarter shares its people’s pleas to protect the lifegiver and spores. Its Flaming Touch outside combat and Fireball in a fight mark it as the group’s fire wielder.
Temple A is one of the three large spires in En'kilah's Temple City that Chieftain Wintergale's shroud mission asks the player to scout.
Temple B is one of the three large spires in En'kilah's Temple City that Chieftain Wintergale's shroud mission asks the player to scout.
Temple C is one of the three large spires in En'kilah's Temple City that Chieftain Wintergale's shroud mission asks the player to scout.

Mobu is a Warsong mechanic trying to get the landing’s tanks working, and he needs proper tools and parts to repair them. He warns that the mist is dangerous and says he will not go near it. Though he asks after Warsong supplies, he is unhappy in uniform and says he wants to leave the Horde.

Waltor of Pal’ea is a Tuskarr survivor of the Kvaldir’s destruction of his home and people. He seeks the return of their stolen relics and calls for justice, while explaining that Tuskarr magic resembles shamanism but serves the elements differently. He recounts the Kvaldir lieutenant Orabus’s role in the attack and urges resistance to the invaders.

At Fizzcrank Airstrip, Crafty Wobblesprocket is a resourceful tinkerer with an informal, impatient manner. She builds experimental tools, including a blaster to shrink magnataur and a screwdriver to reprogram robots, and wants help testing them. Her supplies and tools matter to her work.

This imprisoned Beryl sorcerer serves Malygos and treats the Kirin Tor and their allies as enemies. Under questioning, he angrily refuses to reveal where Lady Evanor is held, then pleads for release while insisting he knows nothing useful.
Kvaldir Mistweavers are combatants that cast Mist of Strangulation. When one is drawn into combat, it stops flying.

Librarian Normantis is a Kirin Tor librarian on Amber Ledge. Bound by the Kirin Tor's code of conduct, he turns to an outsider to use whatever measures are needed to question an imprisoned sorcerer about Lady Evanor's location. He treats the intelligence as urgent and returns to organizing the shelves while the interrogation proceeds.
A crawler found in several areas around Amber Ledge in the Borean Tundra.
A sand turtle found near Amber Ledge in the Borean Tundra.
A Wooly Rhino Matriarch found across several Borean Tundra areas. Its recorded behavior includes a defensive hide response when attacked.
A young Wooly Rhino found in the Borean Tundra near Amber Ledge.
A male Wooly Rhino found in several areas of the Borean Tundra.
The East En'kilah Cauldron is one of three plague cauldrons in the Temple City. It is treated as a Scourge weapon, and Sage Aeire's totem is used near it to neutralize its contents.
The Central En'kilah Cauldron is one of three plague cauldrons in the Temple City. It is treated as a Scourge weapon, and Sage Aeire's totem is used near it to neutralize its contents.
The West En'kilah Cauldron is one of three plague cauldrons in the Temple City. It is treated as a Scourge weapon, and Sage Aeire's totem is used near it to neutralize its contents.

A Kvaldir Mist Lord threatens land dwellers and speaks of subjugating people as a source of prolonged amusement. Its battle cries promise burning and ash, giving this mist shaper a cruel, openly hostile manner.
Aspatha is the Broodmother.
The Gammoth Tender has a tending role associated with Gammoth.
Elder Mootoo is Mootoo the Younger's father, whom she senses nearby while seeking escape from the mist. His dialogue describes the Kvaldir beyond it and says the area was condemned by Hellscream.

Mootoo the Younger is searching for her father in the mist, sensing his aura nearby. Her scripted lines ask for help against the monsters, voice worry about finding him, and express relief when she does.

Rocknar is a hostile elemental that treats outsiders as a threat to the land, warning that they are not welcome and must be removed. It threatens to freeze and destroy intruders and retreats into an ice block when the fight ends.

Snow Tracker Grumm is a badly weakened taunka tracker who has fallen into Scourge hands. He warns that captives are being bled to feed a blood prince, then asks for the blood globes to be destroyed and word carried to Junek. His speech falters as he collapses, and he barely responds when found.
A Skadir runecaster among the Kvaldir attacking Riplash, wielding the Rune of Retribution. Veehja seeks runecasters among the raiders who devastated her people.

A Skadir Longboatsman is one of the Kvaldir, the giant mist-men feared by the tuskarr. This fighter taunts survivors and speaks of sending prisoners to fight in pairs for their lives, showing a cruel, theatrical side to the Kvaldir's violence.
A Skadir Raider is a Kvaldir attacker, counted among the mist-men who destroyed Karuk's village. Its battle cries threaten to draw victims' souls into the mist and urge them to be consumed by it.
A Skadir Mariner is a Kvaldir fighter among the barbaric enemies Veehja seeks revenge against at Riplash. In combat, it uses Demoralizing Shout and Uppercut.
An En'kilah Blood Globe holds blood drained from prisoners and taken to the necropolis to feed the blood prince. Grumm asks that these globes be destroyed.
A Scourged Flamespitter is a flying Scourged attacker around Valiance Keep. Some of these fliers get over the front lines and strike the inner defenses; reinforced nets can knock them from the sky.

Inquisitor Salrand is a hostile figure at Beryl Point who reacts angrily to interruptions and calls intruders cowards. She has destroyed a key and declares that the captured archmage belongs to Malygos.
A Beryl mage hunter encountered around Beryl Point, this hostile combatant uses Frost Cut against opponents.

Bonker Togglevolt is a captive who came to parlay with the snobolds, but was chained up for the snobolds’ shaman Kaganishu to feed to Magmothregar. He protests that he is not an appetizer and resents being chained, then urges his rescuer to hurry to safety. At the airstrip, he says he can continue alone and asks that Fizzcrank be told he is back safely.

Fizzcrank Fullthrottle leads the airstrip and its missions. He says he should have flown a recent reconnaissance mission himself because leading it was his responsibility, and he still trusts and misses his former wingman, Iggy “Tailspin” Cogtoggle. He directs newcomers to his second-in-command, Jinky Wingnut, to handle matters after hearing his account of the Mechagnomes.
An infected kodo beast afflicted by Scourge infection. It can be cured and saved; an individual animal is Torp's kodo.

Prince Valanar is identified as a San'layn prince at Naxxanar. He sits within the necropolis's upper reaches, defended by his lieutenants Vanthryn the Merciless and Luthion the Vile. The taunka seek his defeat for their people's safety. In combat, he uses Shadow Bolt and Soul Blast.

Greatmother Taiga is a Taunka elder at Taunka'le Village who sends others to investigate mysteries and threats affecting her people. She considers the mechagnomes dangerous, yet wants their captured souls released and questioned to learn what happened. The news of her grandson Bristlehorn's death visibly grieves her; she honors his death and thanks those who carry out his last wishes.

Sage Highmesa is a Taunka sage whose curiosity about the Scourge structure that fell near the Dens of Dying led her north before a full party could accompany her. Investigating the plague afflicting the magnataur, she offers cleansing seeds and asks travelers to destroy Scourge threats. She worries about the impetuous Longrunner Bristlehorn and asks that Greatmother Taiga be told she will follow shortly.
Hamat is an old female beast known to Sage Highmesa, who asks visitors to keep their voices down because Hamat needs her rest.

Farmer Torp tends sick kodos at Warsong Farms Outpost and is working on a cure while asking for help against the unliving swine attacking them. He calls the kodos his babies and worries about their survival; his medicine and riding snaffle are practical tools for rescuing them. He also says the recovered kodos will help soldiers and journeymen strengthen their presence in Northrend.
An En'kilah necrolord of the Cult of the Damned; in combat, this caster uses Bone Armor.
A Scourge prisoner held in a cage on the farmland near Warsong Farms Outpost. When freed, the prisoner expresses heartfelt gratitude.
A Warsong Aberration found around En'kilah, this creature attacks nearby foes with Thrash Kick.
A Skadir Mistweaver among the Kvaldir attacking Veehja's people at Riplash; in combat, it uses Mist of Strangulation.
A magnataur afflicted by the plague at the Dens of Dying, where the creatures shelter in caves. It fights with a Plague Cloud.
Farshire Militia patrols are summoned to follow one of several routes through the area.
Varidus the Flenser is a Cult of the Damned necrolord who declares the Lich King unstoppable. He mocks the Horde and its heroes, urging them to accept the world's destruction.
A Nerub'ar warrior that uses Rush to close on foes in combat.
A Nerub'ar tunneler that shields itself with Rock Shield in combat.
A Harvest Collector encountered in Farshire that attacks with Claw Slash in combat.
Infested prisoners are found in the area and summon another creature when they die.
A Tuskarr prisoner captured by the Kvaldir was forced to fight the other captives. After being saved, he says Karuk is still alive and asks that the youngling be told his father fought to the end.
A Plagued Scavenger is one of the Scourge threats faced by Farshire's militia. It attacks with an infected bite.
A cultist necrolyte that resumes shadow channelling when it returns.
Longrunner Bristlehorn is an individual companion at Talramas whom his expedition expects back. His companion calls him impetuous; when found, Bristlehorn says he is not long for this world.
A festering ghoul, one of the Lich King's Scourge at the fallen necropolis of Talramas and the surrounding pools.
A vengeful spirit identified as Taunka, appearing among the Scourge-haunted lands of Northrend.
A Tundra Wolf found around Borean Tundra can be tracked by the blood it leaves behind: on death, it casts Animal Blood.

Doctor Razorgrin is a hostile doctor at the Dens of Dying who treats intruders as fresh meat and parts, even recommending evisceration. His combat barks pair that menace with clinical bravado; outside combat, he casts Defibrillate, fitting his grisly medical work.
Marsh caribou are animal creatures found across several areas of the Borean Tundra. They cast Animal Blood when they die.

Lich-Lord Chillwinter is a hostile undead presence in the Dens of Dying. He is named as a target alongside Doctor Razorgrin, and on aggression he cries, “Die!” or “Filthy breather!” His other recorded line warns, “You cannot stop us!”
Talramas Abominations are undead creatures in the Dens of Dying. In combat, this abomination uses Plague Cloud.
Gorloc Waddlers are gorloc creatures found in the Borean Tundra. This type uses Gorloc Stomp in combat.
Gorloc Gibberers are gorloc creatures found in the Borean Tundra. This type uses Deep Dredge in combat.
Gorloc Steam Belchers are gorloc creatures found in the Borean Tundra. This type uses Belch Blast in combat.
A Gorloc Mud Splasher is a beast identified by the Gorloc name and the Mud Splasher role.
A Gorloc Hunter is a Gorloc beast whose combat routine uses Paralyzing Slime.
A humanoid bearing the designation Gorloc Dredger.

Mordle Cogspinner works on the transmatter at Fizzcrank Airstrip, trying to restore outgoing teleport and align its incoming ports. He asks for spare parts from the Scalding Pools, Geyser Fields, and pumping station, and worries about another accident. His boss Tinky went east with Bixie Wrenchshanker; Mordle says Tinky is the only one who can fix the outgoing unit. He also tells of King Mrgl-Mrgl, leader of the displaced Winterfin murlocs, seeking help.

Bixie Wrenchshanker is investigating the plague among the magnataur near the Dens of Dying. After she and Tinky went to stalk the magnataur, she discovered that the caves held cultists spreading the plague. She devised a powder from her usual anti-poison mixture and other ingredients to neutralize their concoction, and recruits help to contain the threat.

Warbringer Goredrak is an Azure-Lord of the Blue Dragonflight and one of Malygos' trusted underlings. Raelorasz identifies him as holding an energy core sought for a prison fragment connected with Malygos' captured mages and other arcane entities. Goredrak uses arcane attacks and drains power in combat.
Blue Drakonid Supplicants are dragonkin whose name marks them as supplicants. They can cast Power Sap in combat.

Tinky Wickwhistle is the airstrip’s chief transmatter engineer. After exploring the crashed necropolis, she was captured by its cultists and planned to build a port device from scavenged parts to escape. She believes her evil twin ended up somewhere colder and asks for word to be taken to Bixie Wrenchshanker. Her first attempt to activate the device leaves her feeling lighter.

General Cerulean is a Coldarra commander among Malygos’s trusted underlings. Raelorasz’s search for fragments of a prison points to Cerulean as a possible source of its casing. He channels arcane energy and uses Frost Shock in combat.
Coldarra Scalesworn are dragonkin encountered in Coldarra. They use Frost Nova and Rend in combat.
Coldarra Mage Slayers are demon creatures found in Coldarra. Their name identifies them as mage hunters.
A Coldarra Spellbinder and one of the underlings Raelorasz says hold the drake-runes he needs for translation. It casts Frostbolt in combat.

Raelorasz calls Caleras a Kirin Tor traitor and believes he may have an Azure Codex needed to interpret the blue drakes’ runes; he also says Caleras’s underlings hold those runes. Caleras uses Frostbolt and Frost Nova in combat and Arcane Channeling out of combat.
An Arcane Serpent found in Coldarra’s surrounding areas; it attacks with Arcane Jolt.
A Coldarra Spellweaver singled out by Raelorasz as a target in the war against Malygos. It casts Arcane Missiles in combat and Arcane Channeling out of combat.
An Ascended Mage Hunter.

Chieftain Gurgleboggle is named alongside Chieftain Burblegoggle as one of the chieftains from whom the two halves of the Horn of Elemental Fury are sought. The quest text presents the horn’s tale as a legend whose truth is uncertain.
Chieftain Burblegobble is a humanoid identified by this chieftain title and name, in Coldarra.
Warmage Moran is a warmage in Coldarra.
Coldarra Wyrmkin are dragonkin found across two areas of Coldarra. They use Frostbite Weapon in combat.

Shadowstalker Getry is a Horde-aligned elite at Warsong Farms. He undertakes a mission against Varidus the Flenser with the player, then speaks with deep respect about fighting beside Saurfang and directs the player back to Warsong Hold.
Warmage Preston is a warmage in Coldarra.
Warmage Austin is a warmage in Coldarra.

Supply Master Taz'ishi handles poison and reagent supplies at Winterfin Retreat. The greeting is casual and welcoming, inviting visitors to ask what they need; the vendor menu offers browsing of goods.
Airman Skyhopper is a named airman associated with the Fizzcrank Airstrip. Travelers are pointed toward Fizzcrank Fullthrottle there for an urgent report about threats near the airstrip.
The Wooly Mammoth Bull is an animal found in the Borean Tundra. It casts Animal Blood when it dies.

Jinky Wingnut is an engineer at Fizzcrank Airstrip involved in efforts against Gearmaster Mechazod. Jinky asks for help restoring infected mechagnomes, then expresses relief and gratitude when the treatment works. Jinky also directs the effort to dismantle Mechazod's lieutenants and prepare for the confrontation, showing concern for the people threatened by the Gearmaster.
Scavenge-bot 004-A8 is a mechanical scavenger operating around the oil-stricken coast. Its combat system uses a cutting laser, marking it as an active machine rather than an ordinary animal.

Sentry-bot 57-K is an automated guard that detects intruders and threatens assimilation or elimination. Its warnings and call to repel intruders frame it as a security machine, not a source of local conversation or diplomacy.
Defendo-tank 66D is a defensive machine that reacts to incoming fliers by calling for them to be shot down. Its combat warning gives it an active guard role.
A Kvaldir raider belongs to the force attacking Kaskala from the mists. Ataika calls the assault unprovoked and asks for help fighting them.
A Kaskala Defender is one of the defenders associated with the Kaskala community. Defenders are found across nearby coastal areas and fight with thrown weapons.
A Fizzcrank pilot in the Geyser Fields, this humanoid is present at the airstrip area.
Known as the Den Mother, Rockfang is a creature in the Geyser Fields. In combat she uses Chilling Howl; when she dies, she casts Animal Blood.

Abner Fizzletorque is a Fizzcrank engineer working to collapse Nerubian tunnels with a machine built from an old bot. He seeks sinkhole reconnaissance, oil fuel and mammoth hides to complete it. His dialogue is practical and pressed for time: he promises compensation, then remarks that the hide cleaning will add to the work already waiting.

Archmage Evanor thanks the visitor as a friend of Dalaran and acknowledges their recent deeds. She says the local menace will be dealt with, then urges them toward the urgent crisis west of the ledge, directing them to Lord Surristrasz for details.

Lady Evanor is the mage rescued from captivity at Beryl Point. After her release, she receives the hero at the mage tower on Amber Ledge and offers sincere thanks; her next concern is an urgent crisis west of the ledge, for which she sends them to Lord Surristrasz.
Friar Tuskus is a humanoid in Borean Tundra.

Gammothra leads the magnataur den at Gammoth and controls its population, making the leader a threat that Primal Mighthorn wants stopped before an uprising. Mighthorn's plan is to weaken Gammothra with crushed bloodspore flower, then slay the den leader and return the head as proof.
This is a living wolf stained with oil, one of many found in the same area. When it returns, it casts Oil Coat, renewing the coating that marks it out.
Scavenge-bot 005-B6 is a numbered mechanical unit equipped with a cutting laser. It fires the laser in combat.
55-D Collect-a-tron is a mechanical construct that dumps oil at close range.
Bloodmage Alkor is a blood mage encountered in the Borean Tundra.

In Hierophant Cenius's account, Clam Master K styles himself master of clams, a claim she condemns. She asks that he be found at wreckage off the Abandoned Reach; in a fight, he uses a hooked net at close range and throws spears from farther away.
Kaw is known as the Mammoth Destroyer and taunts challengers to face him and feel his thunder. A hunt tied to his name concerns the slaughter of mammoths and his coveted war halberd.

Zaza's account describes Karen “I Don't Caribou” the Culler as the treacherous leader of the caribou trappers, mocking slain animals and drinking their blood; Zaza warns that she is well armed and guarded. In combat she uses cleave, whirlwind, and intercept.

Harold Lane, called the Fur Baron, is identified by D.E.H.T.A. as the man directing Nesingwary's operations in the Borean Tundra and held responsible for mass slaughter in Nagrand. He is a hunter who mocks an attempt to deafen him with the Cenarion horn, then reacts to its sound; in combat he uses a bear trap.

Loot Crazed Poachers are violent hunters who call killing a sport and threaten to kill their quarry. One boasts that "ol' Hemet" can make use of a victim's bones, tying the group to Hemet's hunting operation. They stalk under stealth before attacking.

Iggy "Tailspin" Cogtoggle is an injured Fizzcrank squadron commander stranded after a flash brought his squadron down. He feels responsible for recovering the fallen pilots' insignia and finishing the wreck-scuttling protocol to keep Fizzcrank technology from Horde-aligned goblins. He also seeks mission microfilm swallowed by wolves, using bait made from gorloc spices. Though his injuries make it dangerous to leave the wreckage, he persists in completing his duties and hopes to return to Fizzcrank to report and honor the dead.

D.E.H.T.A. Enforcers confront people they accuse of harming animals. One challenges a visitor covered in animal blood, calling them a butcher or calf killer and threatening death; their lines show their fierce opposition to animal slaughter.

Arch Druid Lathorius is a D.E.H.T.A. druid who champions the humane treatment of animals in the Borean Tundra. He regards hunters who harm wildlife as enemies and is especially distressed by trapped or orphaned mammoth calves. He mobilizes allies against Nesingwary's hunters and Harold Lane's operation, reflecting his fierce commitment to protecting the region's animals.

Hierophant Cenius is a D.E.H.T.A. hierophant at the Borean Tundra encampment, fiercely opposed to Nesingwary’s pearl and hunting trade. Cenius argues that the clams’ habitat and other animals must be protected, rejects the claim that anyone can be master of sea creatures, and directs missions against those profiting from their slaughter. The blunt, accusatory reaction to animal blood reflects this uncompromising stance.

Zaza is a D.E.H.T.A. activist at the Borean Tundra encampment, focused on the caribou harmed by Nesingwary’s trappers. Zaza recalls when the animals roamed peacefully and condemns their constant panic and suffering. Zaza urges the player to turn the trappers’ own traps against them, then targets their leader, Karen, for the violence done to the animals. Zaza frames this work as serving the Earth Mother and shows little sympathy for the trappers.

Killinger is a D.E.H.T.A. den watcher whose rebukes condemn anyone who harms the animals in his care, calling attackers of young rhinos calf killers and butchers. Though D.E.H.T.A. rarely seeks an animal's death, he supports killing Nedar's tainted rhino companion as well as the hunter who preys on vulnerable rhinos.
Fizzcrank Mechagnomes speak as a collective and declare resistance futile. Their lines praise machinery over flesh, promise technological enhancement, and boast that they can remove curses.

Sergeant Hammerhill helps organize Valiance Keep's defense against the Scourge, urging renowned fighters to bolster the front and using practical measures against threats from land, air, and underground. His replies stress the danger of being overrun and credit an ally's help with buying the keep time to fight another day.
Oiled Fledgelings are young, oil-stained birds found in the Borean Tundra.
A D.E.H.T.A. enforcer in Borean Tundra who turns fiercely against those marked by animal blood, accusing them of killing calves and attacking them as butchers and murderers.

Medic Hawthorn treats a soldier poisoned by cryptfiends and urgently seeks anti-venom to save him. Hawthorn has slowed the poison but needs supplies from the Stormbreaker, and warns that the soldier's recovery will take time. Hawthorn's experience treating people from every station informs a conviction that death makes them equal.

Vindicator Yaala investigates the Cult of the Damned and has learned its secret language. Working with evidence from Harbinger Vurenn, Yaala directs a trusted operative to investigate the cult discreetly, then uses an oculus to expose its disguised agents in Valiance Keep. Yaala remains wary that the cult can hide in plain sight.

Tom Hegger is a Cult of the Damned operative hiding behind a fisherman's cover to avoid military duty. When exposed, he invokes Arthas for strength, threatens death, and vows to fight rather than go quietly.

Guard Mitchells presents himself as a Valiance Keep guard, but the cover hides a Cult of the Damned operative. When exposed, he drops the charade, invokes Arthas for strength, and threatens anyone who confronts him, resolved not to go down quietly.
Marsh Fawns are young deer found throughout the Borean Tundra marshes. When one dies, it casts Animal Blood.

Nesingwary Trappers work the hunters’ operation in the Borean Tundra caribou grounds, pursuing hides and setting traps. Their chatter mocks the animals as beasts and celebrates the rewards: supposed self-skinned hides, meat, and a set of Nesingwary steak knives.

Loot Crazed Divers harvest pearls from Lake Kum’uya’s freshwater giant clam beds as part of Nesingwary’s pearl-farming operation. Their chatter celebrates the clams’ contents and even imagines pearl goods; when badly wounded, they become crazed. D.E.H.T.A. condemns the operation as a threat to this rare habitat.

Hierophant Liandra of D.E.H.T.A. works at the Abandoned Reach to stop animal-part shipments, accusing Nesingwary's hunters and the Northsea Freebooters of a murderous trade. She asks for recovered remains so the animals can receive a proper burial. Her condemnation of animal killers is fierce, including threats against those she calls butchers and calf killers.
A Northsea mercenary is a hired fighter identified with the Northsea.
The Fizzcrank Recon Pilot did not survive their squadron's crash; searches of the body focus on the pilot's emergency toolkit and insignia.
A Northsea thug encountered in the Northsea area, identified by the thug role.
A Northsea thug encountered in the Northsea area, identified by the thug role.

Fezzix Geartwist is a goblin tinkerer at Taunka'le Village, trying to rebuild a crashed gnomish flying machine. He salvages what he can, asks for toolkits and steam-cured hides to continue the work, and tests his repairs with anxious optimism. He celebrates a working attempt with Dorain, then cries out in pain and gives up after the flight goes wrong.
Trapped mammoth calves are caught in hunters' traps in the northern tundra. D.E.H.T.A. asks that they be freed, and a rescued calf trumpets in approval.

Khu'nok is an ancient, wise mammoth of the Borean Tundra who can care for orphaned calves. Khu'nok recognizes help given to the mammoth kin and considers the player an ally, while believing Kaw must die to end their torment.
A member of Kaw's forces in the Borean Tundra, this combatant uses Destructive Strike.
Moria is Kaw's War Mammoth, a named animal that can carry a passenger.
"Lunchbox" is the rhino companion Nedar raised as his mount and bodyguard. D.E.H.T.A. describes the animal as tainted and calls for it to be killed alongside Nedar.
Ambassador Talonga is waiting to speak with the chieftain, but Taunka'le cannot wait for help. He asks a capable traveler to aid his people and sends them to Sage Earth and Sky at Taunka'le Village.

The Loot Crazed Hunter treats killing as sport and hunts for profit. He boasts that Hemet can use a victim's bones, wants more hooves to buy a new gun, and eagerly bargains for rhino-head helmets. He threatens prey for its hide and jokes about veal, while mocking Nesingwary's spending and Lane's judgment.
A Scourged Footman is an undead combatant that fights with Mortal Strike.

Sage Earth and Sky is a Taunka sage at Taunka'le Village, distrustful of the gnomes whose inventions foul the land. He says his people plan to leave for Icemist after breaking through the Scourge, but first wants the threat from the gnomes' machines addressed. He teaches a visitor to master the storm, then provides a lightning rod to weaken the robots while sparing the mechagnomes for Greatmother Taiga's plans.

Dorain Frosthoof is an apprentice wind tamer who trusts the enduring power of the elements more than Fezzix's unreliable machinery. He gives Fezzix a windsoul totem to gather energy from steam ragers and intends to use its charge to demonstrate how elemental power can solve the engine problem. He is still an apprentice, not yet a full wielder of that power.
A crashed Fizzcrank recon pilot is one of the dead gnomes whose possessions hold an emergency toolkit. Its rations, tools and duct tape may help Fezzix reassemble the gnomish flying machines.
An ore cart used on the rails. When released, it squeaks against them as it starts moving.

Durkot Wolfbrother is a stable master who introduces himself as protector of the pack. He offers pet stabling and can arrange worg transport. His greeting presents him as responsible for the pack, while his stable and transport services connect him to its care and travel.
A Warsong worg.
A Storm Totem that summons a Storm Tempest when addressed.

High Priest Talet-Kha is one of the Scourge leader's lieutenants at En'kilah, where the priests command Scourge forces. His scroll from the Spire of Pain is sought as a key to Naxxanar. He reacts angrily when disturbed during meditation.

High Priest Naferset is one of the Scourge leader's lieutenants at En'kilah, where the priests command Scourge forces. His scroll from the Spire of Decay is sought as a key to Naxxanar. He protests when interrupted before finishing his feast.
Blakelow is a humanoid associated with Nogg's Machine Shop.

Gerald Green is a Farshire settler helping organize its defense as the Scourge overrun the settlement. He calls on others to aid the militia and describes the defenders as ordinary miners, farmers and craftsmen forced to fight for their land.

Jeremiah Hawning once oversaw Farshire's harvest golems. After the Scourge destroyed much of the farmland, he hopes to rewire the harvest collectors for defense, though he admits he needs his manual and is still learning. The work matters to him: completing it makes him feel useful again.

Wendy Darren fears the Scourge plague may have reached Farshire's grain and urges settlers to burn it before survivors can eat it. She is determined to defend the new lives the settlers built in Northrend and accepts the loss of the grain as a necessary precaution.
A Darkfallen Deathblade of the San'layn, this undead combatant uses Death Coil and Icy Touch in battle.

Iron Eyes is a taunka concerned that gnomish machinery is polluting the land. She asks travelers to gather spare parts from the pools so she can see them properly disposed of before the taunka leave for Icemist. She says caring for the land is necessary for the taunka to live in harmony with it.
An off-duty battleguard.

Librarian Serrah is a Dalaran-trained scholar serving at the Transitus Shield outpost on Coldarra. With supply lines cut and food running low, she helps sustain the outpost’s warmages by finding provisions and improvising mana supplies. She also asks for news of Corastrasza to reach her worried brother, Raelorasz.
Bor'gorok Peon is a peon worker associated by name with Bor'gorok, found in the Borean Tundra.
Darkfallen bloodbearers are undead members of the San'layn that follow a patrol route at a walk.

Raelorasz is a leader in the resistance to Malygos at the Transitus Shield, coordinating assaults and efforts to rescue captured allies. He studies the fragments of a powerful prison and hopes its captive may aid the cause. His concern for young drakes and warm welcome to Keristrasza show ties to the dragonflights.
A hostile bone warrior is an undead combatant that attacks mortals and uses Sunder Armor in battle.
A Nexus drake hatchling is a young drake capable of using Netherbreath in combat.
Mark Hanes is a questgiver associated with the appeal to find Leryssa at the Valiance Keep inn. He says she is asking for help and seems desperate, though she does not know the adventurer.
A Taunka'le Brave is a humanoid combatant found around Taunka'le and elsewhere in the Borean Tundra. In combat, this brave uses Ground Slam.

Mother Tauranook has called for Taunka'le's evacuation as the Scourge closes in. She sends her people toward Icemist and mourns leaving the village where they lived for generations; the loss of the snow signals that their time there has ended, though she hopes they may return.
Taunka'le Evacuees are humanoid taunka identified by their flight from Taunka'le. They appear around the village and nearby Borean Tundra.
The Taunka'le Pack Kodo is a beast associated with Taunka'le, found around the village and nearby Borean Tundra.

Ataika is a Kaskala warrior who sees the Kvaldir attack as an unprovoked assault on a sacred place tied to the Tuskarr ancestors and Tayutka. He urges an outsider to fight beside his people, while arguing that warriors can be replaced but wise elders cannot; he is especially concerned for Muahit, the stubborn shaman at Tayutka’s altar. Ataika also recognizes the mark of Karkut, guardian of the dead, and invokes Karkut in remembrance of the fallen.

Thassarian was forced to serve Arthas as a death knight and now seeks vengeance for what Arthas did to him. He pursues knowledge from a captured lich and works against the Cult of the Damned, whose orders lead back to Naxxanar. He is deeply concerned for his sister Leryssa and rejoices when she is safe, though he tells her he is not yet done with the Scourge. He says his obligations to his king and army are fulfilled and that he will follow his own heart and fight no wars but his own.

High Deathpriest Isidorus serves the Cult of the Damned. He says he and his men are kept in the dark and that their orders come from Naxxanar. When confronted by a death knight, he begs for mercy, recognizes the knight as someone once among the cultists, and pleads to be spared from the knight's minion.
A slain member of the Cult of the Damned.

Thassarian seeks Tanathal’s hidden phylactery to obtain knowledge from him. In that account, Tanathal is a lich whose soul is stored outside his body, preventing Thassarian from forcing answers through physical pain alone.

Lurid offers an unnamed master to kill a priest painfully and taunts a weak opponent to beg for life. Lurid threatens those who serve Arthas but tells an ally that working together could become agreeable.

Private Casey reports surviving a Scourge ambush after landing and discovering a Cult of the Damned spy among the expedition. Worried by Thassarian’s evidence of wider infiltration, Casey seeks Courier Lanson, a trusted messenger sent to western Dragonblight who has not returned, fearing he may have fallen to the Scourge.

Corporal Venn holds Death's Stand with a small force ordered to take the Wailing Ziggurat. Outnumbered, injured and without an escape route, he asks for help pushing back the undead around it. He regards Thassarian as a good ally despite his past as a death knight, and hopes Valiance Keep will send reinforcements.

A Cult of the Damned member fleeing the Wailing Ziggurat, this cultist cries that it has been lost and urges others to run to the temple. The lines convey panic and continued allegiance to Arthas as the cultist fears the death knight.
Dusk is a demon in Borean Tundra.

Ziggurat Defenders are undead circling the Wailing Ziggurat and pressing the small force at Death's Stand. Venn asks for them to be driven back to ease the pressure on his people as they hold their position.

Utaik is a tuskarr of Kaskala facing the loss of his home and people to the sons of the mist and Karkut's spirit. He says Kaskala's families have been sent to Unu'pe while the remaining tuskarr fight, and asks for supplies to feed their relatives there if Kaskala falls.

Elder Muahit is Kaskala’s most venerable shaman and one of its elders. He is stubbornly devoted to the settlement and its spirits, refusing to abandon Kaskala’s altar even as the Kvaldir attack. He believes Issliruk’s guidance can save his people, and speaks of Tayutka and Karkut as guardians of survivors and the dead. Iruk is his nephew; Muahit asked him to retrieve Issliruk’s totem, and grieves that the Kvaldir killed him. Muahit resists Ataika’s call to flee, while still believing Kaskala may survive.

Iruk is Elder Muahit’s young tuskarr nephew. The Kvaldir killed him while he was carrying out Muahit’s request to retrieve Issliruk’s totem, and his body fell into the water north of Njord’s Breath Bay. A search of his corpse can recover the totem; he appears to have been slain in combat rather than drowned.

Captain Jacobs is the officer whom Gerald Green accuses of taking the cart-release key when the military entered the Farshire mine. Gerald suspects the plague affecting the soldiers may have affected Jacobs as well. In combat, Jacobs uses Blade Flurry and Mortal Strike.

Elder Muahit identifies Heigarr the Horrible as the Kvaldir leader threatening Kaskala from Njord's Breath Bay. Muahit believes the storm's confusion can turn the battle against Heigarr. In combat, Heigarr uses Cleave and Concussion Blow.

Karuk identifies Gamel the Cruel as the leader of the raiding party that killed Karuk's father, and says Gamel made his home in a cave on the beach at Riplash Strand. In combat, Gamel uses Mortal Strike.

Veehja names Ragnar Drakkarlund as the captain deep inside northeastern Riplash and says he holds the golden Trident of Naz'jan. Veehja describes the raiders sacrificing naga and tuskarr to awaken Leviroth, and seeks vengeance for Veehja's people. In combat, Ragnar uses Whirlwind.

An aquatic beast imprisoned in Riplash during Raj Naz'jan's reign, Leviroth is described as having escaped and is hunted with Azshara's Trident of Naz'jan. When struck by the Impale Leviroth spell, it casts Leviroth Self-Impale and Cosmetic - Underwater Blood.

Nargo Screwbore is the Durotar Zeppelin Master. His directions identify the Mighty Wind as the link from this station to Durotar, and his announcement calls travelers aboard when the zeppelin to Orgrimmar arrives.

Nelno Copperbeam is a dockmaster whose directions point travelers missing the Eastern Kingdoms toward the Kraken's return voyage to Stormwind. He adds a personal note: he would enjoy the warmer weather there.
Agloolik is a dockmaster who identifies the great sea turtle Walker of Waves as traveling from this dock to Moa'ki Harbor in Dragonblight.
"Charlie" Northtop is an innkeeper who welcomes visitors and offers a place to rest. His inn also offers making it one's home and browsing goods, combining lodging with vendor service.
Toby "Mother Goose" Ironbolt is a stable master who offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions. His greeting presents both as practical care for visitors' companions.
Mistie Flitterdawn is the reagent and poison vendor at Fizzcrank Airstrip. Visitors can browse her goods, with reagent and poison sales among her services.
Willis Wobblewheel is a blacksmith at Fizzcrank Airstrip who offers goods for browsing.
Chief Engineer Galpen Rolltie supplies engineering goods. He offers goods for browsing.
A Fizzcrank airman, a humanoid in Borean Tundra.
Kara Thricestar is the air traffic controller at Fizzcrank Airstrip. Her flight menu includes an option to request travel to the Dens of Dying.

This Fizzcrank paratrooper speaks as one of the pilots and presents parachute practice as part of a soldier’s training. The trooper explains a spire exercise involving a teleporter, with another trooper stationed above with parachutes.
Rupert Keeneye is a Fizzcrank watcher whose duty is expressed through patrol. He follows a route and pauses at one point before continuing.
The Fizzcrank Engineering Crew are the outpost’s engineering group, identified collectively rather than through individual names.
A reckless scavenger is an undead creature found in the Borean Tundra. When summoned, it starts attacking, making it a hostile presence rather than a helpful scavenger.
Tewah Chillmane is a leather armor merchant offering goods and repair service to travelers passing through the Borean Tundra.
Pahu Frosthoof is an innkeeper who welcomes visitors in from the cold and offers them a place to rest. Pahu also sells goods, making the inn a hospitable stop for travelers in the Borean Tundra.
Trader Alorn is a general-goods merchant in the Stormwind Reach settlement, where visitors can browse his goods.
Danook Stormwhisper is a trade-goods merchant in the Stormwind Reach settlement. His listed trade role distinguishes him from general-goods vendor Trader Alorn.

Halona Stormwhisper is a stable master who helps visitors stable pets and recover lost companions. Her greeting presents both kinds of assistance, though which options are available can depend on context.
Wind Tamer Oril is a humanoid in Borean Tundra.
Brave Storming Sky is a humanoid in Borean Tundra.
Longrunner Taima is a humanoid in Borean Tundra.
Snow Tracker Haloke is a humanoid snow tracker in the Borean Tundra.
Taunka'le Longrunner is a humanoid longrunner found in several parts of the Borean Tundra.
Omu Spiritbreeze is a wind rider master who offers fast travel. When attacked, Omu calls for guards, and an enraged wyvern is summoned.
Kimbiza is a wind rider master who offers fast travel. When attacked, Kimbiza calls for guards, and an enraged wyvern is summoned.
Tomas Riverwell is a gryphon master who offers fast travel. When attacked, he calls for guards, and an enraged gryphon is summoned.
Groll deals in general goods, and visitors can browse his wares.
Brokkan Bear-Arms handles trade goods, giving this Warsong Hold merchant a distinct supply role.
Zend'li Venomtusk specializes in poison supplies.
Drikka supplies reagents, serving a different need from the general, trade, and poison goods sold by nearby merchants.
Raenah is a Grand Master Tailoring Trainer. She offers to teach Cloth Scavenging for a few gold, explaining that it can yield extra Frostweave from slain Northrend humanoids.
Orn Tenderhoof is a Grand Master Cooking Trainer serving the Warsong Offensive, whose warriors need food. He asks for chilled meat from Northrend beasts and offers to teach a stew recipe in return.
Tansy Wildmane is identified as a Grand Master Herbalism Trainer.
Arthur Henslowe is identified as a Grand Master Alchemy Trainer.
Brunna Ironaxe is identified as a Grand Master Mining Trainer.
Adelene Sunlance is a Grand Master Inscription Trainer.
Eorain Dawnstrike is a Grand Master Enchanting Trainer.
Crog Steelspine is identified as a Grand Master Blacksmithing Trainer.

Geba'li is a Grand Master jewelcrafting trainer in Warsong Hold. He says the cold is hard on his bones, but he has learned to cut perfect gems. In his Gem Perfection quest, he asks for Huge Citrines, Dark Jade and Shadow Crystals so he can teach improved cuts for uncommon Northrend gems.
Tiponi Stormwhisper is a Grand Master Skinning Trainer in Northrend.
Falorn Nightwhisper is a Grand Master Alchemy Trainer in Northrend.
Argo Strongstout is a Grand Master Blacksmithing Trainer in Northrend.

At Valiance Keep, Rollick MacKreel is a Grand Master cooking trainer whose work serves the hungry recruits. He asks for chilled meat to make stew and teach its preparation, tying his cooking instruction to the needs of the keep's new arrivals.
Alexis Marlowe is a Grand Master Enchanting Trainer in Northrend.
Sock Brightbolt is a Grand Master Engineering Trainer in Northrend.
Brynna Wilson is a Grand Master First Aid Trainer in Northrend.
Old Man Robert is a Grand Master Fishing Trainer in Northrend.
Kirea Moondancer is a Grand Master Herbalism Trainer in Northrend.
Tink Brightbolt is identified as a Grand Master Inscription trainer.
Awan Iceborn is a Grand Master Leatherworker.
Alestos is a jewelcrafter whose work serves the war effort. He can cut perfect gems from uncommon Northrend stones and teach that technique, extending his craft beyond ordinary gem cutting.
Rosemary Bovard is a Grand Master Leatherworking Trainer in Northrend.
Fendrig Redbeard is a Grand Master Mining Trainer in the Borean Tundra.
Trapper Jack is a Grand Master Skinning Trainer in the Borean Tundra.

Darin Goodstitch is a master tailor whose work includes Cloth Scavenging. He offers instruction in recovering extra Frostweave from Northrend humanoids, turning tailoring toward practical wartime supplies.
Celidh Aletracker is a stable master who handles pet stabling and helps recover lost companions. The stable keeps her busy, and she also directs a horse to the stable boy for care.
Broff Bombast is a general-goods merchant.
Beem Goldsprocket is a trade-goods merchant. His service is selling trade goods.
Warmage Adami is a flight master.
Korag Keeneye is a general-goods merchant. His services cover general goods and ammunition, setting his stock apart from Vrok’s trade-goods service in the same area.
